props.title: Cyborg

sections.content: Cyborg launched during the peak of post-apocalyptic sci-fi, combining martial arts with dystopian wasteland aesthetics. Jean-Claude Van Damme stars as Gibson Rickenbacker, a "slinger" protecting humanity's last hope against a plague. Director Albert Pyun, known for low-budget sci-fi like Nemesis (1992), created a gritty vision despite severe budget constraints. The film shares DNA with Mad Max 2: The Road Warrior (1981), featuring similar desert wastelands and savage gangs, while incorporating elements from Japanese cyberpunk like Tetsuo: The Iron Man (1989).

sections.content: The late 80s and early 90s saw an explosion of low-budget cyberpunk and post-apocalyptic hybrids. Class of 1999 (1990) merged teen films with killer cyborg teachers, while Split Second (1992) combined cyber-noir with monster horror. These films reflected Cold War anxieties and growing technophobia, often featuring lone warriors fighting against mechanized threats to humanity. SUBHEAD: Martial Arts Meets Cyberpunk

Cyborg marked a crucial intersection between martial arts and sci-fi cinema. Van Damme's athletic abilities allowed for dynamic fight sequences that influenced later techno-martial arts films like Universal Soldier (1992) and TC 2000 (1993). The film's success, despite its modest budget, helped establish a template for hybrid action-sci-fi that continued through the 90s with films like Nemesis (1992) and Knights (1993).
